CALIB — marking calibration prompt fragment
nodes.rationale: Encodes anti-inflation AND anti-compression marking policy: state-wide score distributions are given as context only (not a quota), best-fit banding is mandated, and a consistency check reconciles criterion ratings with the holistic score — designed to make the AI mark like a real VCAA assessor rather than a lenient or overly cautious one.

nodes.label: EXAMCTX — exam context prompt fragment
nodes.rationale: Grounds the AI's judgement in real exam constraints (3-hour handwritten exam, ~55-60 minutes per section) so it does not penalise exam-appropriate length or expect take-home polish.

nodes.label: REPORT_A — Section A assessor-report calibration text
nodes.rationale: Encodes 2024-2025 VCAA assessor report guidance for Section A (text response) so the AI rewards/penalises the same features real assessors flagged, rather than generic essay-marking heuristics.

nodes.label: REPORT_B — Section B assessor-report calibration text
nodes.rationale: Encodes 2024-2025 VCAA assessor report guidance for Section B (creating texts) to calibrate marking to real assessor-identified strengths and weaknesses.

nodes.label: REPORT_C — Section C assessor-report calibration text
nodes.rationale: Encodes a skill-ladder (LOW to HIGH) drawn from VCAA assessor reports for Section C (argument analysis), explicitly to reward strategic selection and audience-effect analysis over technique-checklisting.

nodes.label: Precision mode (3x independent marking, median reported)
nodes.rationale: Trade-off deliberately chosen: marks three times independently and reports the median — slower but more reliable than a single pass, and the mark spread across the three passes flags borderline scripts for human review.

Caterpillar/Chrysalis Stimulus Motif
nodes.rationale: The stimulus quote about a caterpillar's inevitable metamorphosis is woven into the piece's own imagery ('like the caterpillar confined within the fecund dark of a chrysalis') rather than quoted superficially, meeting the marking criterion for meaningful stimulus integration.

nodes.label: Rattlesnake Shedding Motif
nodes.rationale: A controlling metaphor (rattlesnake shedding skin, layered rattles) introduced early and resolved at the climax to represent identity formed from layered belonging; used to justify why the piece scores full marks under 'recurring motifs' criteria.

Fixed-title rule for Section B
nodes.rationale: The title selects the Framework and cannot be modified; when a student's shaded box and title disagreed, assessors followed the title, so the guide enforces writing the title first and matching stimulus to the chosen Framework to avoid disqualifying mismatches.

nodes.label: 2025 Report: Section C - Analysis of Argument and Language
Interplay of argument/language/visuals as discriminator
nodes.rationale: Assessors found identification of techniques was common but explaining how sequencing and device interplay served persuasive purpose separated skill levels; the guide teaches strategic selection over exhaustive coverage because time constraints make covering every element impossible.

nodes.label: FNV-hash answer verification scheme
nodes.rationale: Answers are stored as FNV-1a hashes per stage rather than plaintext, and the final code is XOR-decoded using the concatenation of all correct answers as key, so no answer is ever readable in the page source, forcing students to actually read the guide rather than inspect the code.
